title: Perfect complexes are exactly the pseudo-coherent complexes of finite tor dimension, with a bounded projective model
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes an object K^bullet of D(R) and proves the equivalence of two conditions — K^bullet is perfect if and only if it is pseudo-coherent and has finite tor dimension — and further asserts that when these hold and K^bullet has tor amplitude in [a, b], then K^bullet is quasi-isomorphic to a complex E^bullet of finite projective R-modules with E^i = 0 for i outside [a, b] (source lines 18888-18899). The proof notes that (1) implies (2) is clear, quoting the pseudo-coherence and tor-amplitude statements (proof lines 18902-18903). Hence assume (2) and tor amplitude in [a, b]; in particular H^i(K^bullet) = 0 for i > b (proof lines 18904-18905). Choose a complex F^bullet of finite free R-modules with F^i = 0 for i > b and a quasi-isomorphism F^bullet -> K^bullet (proof lines 18906-18908). Set E^bullet = tau_{>=a}F^bullet, so that E^i is finite free except at E^a, which is a finitely presented R-module (proof lines 18909-18910). By the last-term-flat statement E^a is flat, and by the Algebra statement on finitely presented flat modules E^a is finite projective (proof lines 18911-18913). The non-routine content is the cohomological bound H^i = 0 for i > b, which allows a bounded-above finite free model to be chosen, and the truncation at a, which isolates the single term E^a whose projectivity follows from flatness plus finite presentation.
